title: Engineering All-Hands Notes - 2026-04-15
content:
Attendees: Maya Chen (host), Diego Alvarez, Priya Nair, Ben Thompson, Aisha Rahman, ~55 engineers across infra, serving-runtime, private-deployments, console, observability, SRE.

TL;DR:
- Dedicated v2 rollout: gradual rollout started 2026-04-10; first 10 customers on v2; median p95 latency improved ~18% for 2k token workloads. No regressions in quality so far.
- Incident review: brief latency spike on 2026-04-12 affecting hosted-api routes during a cross-region failover; SRE postmortem in progress, mitigation applied.
- Private: onboarding for Acme Financial (pilot) kicked off; first air-gapped deploy scheduled 2026-04-22.
- Roadmap highlights: prioritize batching/caching improvements and developer-facing rollout controls for Q2.

Agenda:
1) Quick metrics snapshot (Maya)
2) Team round-robin updates (7m each)
3) Incident postmortem summary (SRE)
4) Roadmap & prioritization (Product + Eng leads)
5) Hiring/operations & shout-outs
6) Q&A / open issues

1) Metrics snapshot (Maya)\- Platform tokens served last week: ~1.8B (hosted + dedicated).\- 7d rolling median p50/p95 generation latencies (hosted-api text-gen): p50 220ms, p95 1.4s.\- Error rate (HTTP 5xx) for generation endpoints: 0.6% (down from 0.9% two weeks ago).\- Dedicated cluster utilization (avg): 72% across active clusters; headroom for burst configured at 15%.\- Cost-per-token (internal calc): estimated -3% month-over-month improvement due to caching tweaks.

Notes: keep an eye on p95 for long-seq requests (>2k tokens) — some customers still see variability depending on kernel selection on older GPU types.

2) Team updates (round-robin)\- Serving-runtime (Diego):\  * v2 scheduler landed in prod for canary pool; continuous batching improvements showing better small-request latency.\  * KV cache refactor in staging; unit tests + integration harness passing — plan to enable for 50% of traffic next week.\  * Open items: need better heuristics for kernel selection when quantized model variants are requested. Filed JIRA-ENG-5678.\- Platform Engineering (Priya):\  * Autoscaler improvements: scaling cooldown reduced from 60s to 30s for G4 pools, reduced scaling overshoot in tests.\  * Cost attribution pipeline: initial rollout to internal dashboards complete; expect public rollout in two sprints.\  * Blocker: GCP quotas causing flaky e2e tests in CI (infra ticket created).\- Private Deployments (Ben):\  * Acme Financial onboarding: network prep checklist mostly complete; SOC2 support docs updated.\  * On-prem installer: alpha 0.9.1 released with KMS integration; feedback loop with solutions engineering ongoing.\  * Question: how to coordinate maintenance windows with enterprise customers — ops to propose cadence.\- Observability + Console (Aisha):\  * New per-route latency heatmaps shipping in console beta next week.\  * Tracing hooks: low-overhead sampling landed; will reduce sampling rate for low-QPS routes to cut storage.\  * Action item: add cost-per-route breakdown to default dashboards (linked to product request PRD-210).\- Site Reliability (SRE lead, remote):\  * Incident 2026-04-12 summary: root cause was a race in region-failover orchestration, combined with an expired temporary cert on a proxy path. Impact: 12 minutes of elevated latency for ~7% of hosts; no token loss.\  * Mitigations applied: backport fix to failover controller, rotate certs automatically during deploys.\  * Postmortem doc: CONFLUENCE-ENG-1423 (in progress).

3) Incident postmortem summary (SRE)\- Timeline: 04-12 03:02 UTC - automated region failover started for cluster eu-west-2; 03:05 - proxy cert validation failed causing retries and queue buildup; 03:14 - automated throttling triggered; 03:20 - mitigation (cert rotation + controller fix) completed.\- Why it happened: a previously hidden edge case in failover ordering; manual step (temp cert) expired earlier than expected in one region.\- What fixed it: code fix to failover ordering + automated cert refresh + improved alerting (new metric: cert-validity-days).\- Actionable follow-ups: add unit test for failover ordering (owner: SRE), add canary for cert refresh (owner: infra), run tabletop drill next month.

4) Roadmap & prioritization (Product + Eng leads)\- Near term (next 6 weeks):\  * Finish KV cache enable for 50% traffic and monitor quality metrics.\  * Dedicated v2 wider rollout to 50% customers (goal: 2026-05-01).\  * Batching improvements for small requests (Q2 focus).\- Medium term (Q2/Q3):\  * Developer rollout controls (canary/A-B across models) — product+platform partnership.\  * Quantization profiles for LLM families to reduce cost by another ~10%.\- Tradeoffs discussed: pushing Dedicated v2 faster increases risk of unseen regressions; proposed mitigation: expand canary buckets and add an automated rollback policy (work in JIRA-ENG-5612).

5) Hiring / operations / shout-outs\- Hiring: interviewing pipeline for senior infra engineer (3 on-site loop scheduled next week).\- Shout-outs: Kudos to Diego and the serving-runtime team for hitting the v2 scheduler milestone; shout-out to SRE on quick mitigation during 04-12 incident.\- Reminders: update on-call rotations in the shared calendar by EOD 2026-04-16.

6) Q&A and open issues\- Q: Are we tracking latency regressions by model family? A: yes — product and serving runtime maintain a matrix (link: CONFLUENCE-ENG-1290).\- Q: Customer-facing incident communication improvements? A: CS owns customer comms; Eng to provide postmortem summary template for CS (action: Maya to send template).\- Open issue: need better visibility into GPU-specific kernel fallbacks — engineering to draft a spec by 2026-04-22 (owner: Diego).

Action items (owners & due dates):
1) Enable KV cache for 50% traffic and monitor quality metrics (owner: Diego) - due 2026-04-22.
2) Add unit test + integration test for failover ordering (owner: SRE) - due 2026-04-20.
3) Propose enterprise maintenance window cadence (owner: Ben) - due 2026-04-21.\4) Add cost-per-route to default dashboards (owner: Aisha) - due 2026-04-29.\5) Draft GPU kernel fallback visibility spec (owner: Diego) - due 2026-04-22.

Notes to self / rough ideas (informal):
- Consider short-lived model-variant feature flags to make rapid rollbacks safer.\- Could we use synthetic traffic jobs to validate kernel selection on each infra upgrade? Open spike idea.\- Reminder: sync with solutions-engineering before next Acme on-prem run.

Meeting recording: internal link (zoom) - zoom.us/rec/share/ENG-2026-04-15-all-hands (internal access only).

Next all-hands: 2026-04-22 (weekly) - same time.

Attachments: screenshots from console beta (latency heatmaps), draft postmortem (CONFLUENCE-ENG-1423), JIRA-ENG-5612 (dedicated v2 rollout epic).

-- end of notes --
